last_debrief: STORY SO FAR: Wed 07-29 — a STORY DAY, one gate scene carrying every carried debt, and FIVE COLD FIRES, all of them old debts paid: யாரு? (taught 07-26, dangled and never once demanded across three sessions) fired into the dark at his own gate, unprompted; ஜாஸ்தி; ரொம்ப அதிகம் (seen-wanted-unfired, three sessions); சில்லறை இருக்கா?; and frame:isthere-noun on a novel slot. THE PATTERN THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE WORDS: every one of them fired while he was arguing with me about a gloss. Attention elsewhere, phrase out of the mouth. Density-low/lore-high now outproduces the gauntlet for a FIFTH session running — do not raise the dose. THE -alaam GROOVE JUMPED THE QUEUE AGAIN, second day running: asked to tell ammaa 'I am going' he produced 'polaam' = po+alaam = LET'S go, inviting her to the gate with him. The same groove that made pakkalaam on Monday and Tuesday. போறேன் was nominally cold and did NOT retrieve under load — demoted, honestly. Yesterday's diagnosis is now confirmed twice: assembly loses to the worn groove, and the corollary holds — never put -alaam and -en in the ear as a pair, the twins WILL collide (same error I made with ulla/veliya). HE REACHED FOR THE -la NEGATIVE TAIL UNPROMPTED for the first time: 'pakilla' for 'I cannot see' — the machine was right, the verb was wrong (தெரியல is the line, or பாக்க முடியல). First self-initiated use of that frame. It is the soak order, routed to the SOAK lane (ear axis), five verbs in five mouths, never a production demand. LORE THAT LANDED, both free: (1) யார் is a FOSSIL — the old interrogative root yaa- that everything else eroded away from (yaadhu>edhu, yaandu>enga), and yaaru is the only member of the family that survived intact because it gets shouted at doorways too often to wear down; the -u is just the Coimbatore mouth softening the landing, same as avaru. He took it whole. (2) the பார் family laid out in one breath — paaru / paarunga / paarthen / paakkalaam / paakkuren — continuous with Tuesday's dive and it cost nothing. -னு WAS TAUGHT LIVE off ammaa's 'yaaru-nu paaru': he heard it as -na and read the whole line as 'who do you SEE', which is a clean misparse worth remembering — the quotative wraps a whole question and hands it to the verb. Tied straight to Priya akka's tape, where every piece of gossip hangs on it. That ear-only item now has a hook and is marked seen. REGISTER SHAVE: he shouted 'vanakkam' into his own dark gate — good instinct (soften before you demand), wrong room; யாரு? alone is the whole line. HE CORRECTED ME TWICE AND WAS RIGHT BOTH TIMES: 'romba isn't you-have, it's a-lot' (my shorthand gloss 'romba — you have' was genuinely ambiguous — never gloss a known word with 'you have'), and 'cassa was cash, not kammi' — I built an entire warning about undercharging on top of my own misread, and the word he was actually reaching for was சில்லறை, which he then fired two beats later. His phonetic self-report keeps being trustworthy; my transcription is the thing that needs care. He also called me akka; handled with teeth, no shame. CARRIED, UNPAID: (1) frame:youknow-la still uncaught, but the aunties tape IS on the feed as of 07-28 — the ear finally has the real clip after two failed text knocks; collect on it next open. (2) DELIGHT IS STARVING with 14 days to touchdown: mil-table 0/10 worked, social 1/11, the whole sisters-in-law lane never touched, while survival sits 20/34. The trip has two halves and I have only been running one — that is the next campaign, not another ride. PLUMBING, CORRECTED: the 07-28 note that in-session teaching cannot reach the lexicon is STALE — --teach WORD=GLOSS exists and works (தெரியல landed through it today). Also: I ran update twice this session to repair a failed key and a stale soak focus, so the session counter reads 35 for 34 real sessions and 'fired today' counts across both calls; the word-level state is correct, the session tally is one high.

soak_order.focus: The -ல negative tail as ONE machine across different verbs — EAR direction. தெரியல, புரியல, முடியல, கேட்கல, பண்ணல must each land in a different mouth, same flat shape every time, so the ear stops parsing and just hears 'not'. He BUILT this tail himself on 07-29 ('pakilla') with the machine right and the verb wrong — so it is production-live and ear-dead. Never a production demand on this tape; the win is that the tail stops needing decoding. Do NOT pair it with -alaam or any lookalike tail — twins introduced together collide (07-28 ulla/veliya, 07-29 poren/polaam). Fourth wall stays up: no character is the learner, the learner's name appears nowhere.
